editorial.headline: Computer Repair: Nationally Open, PMA-Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This wide computer-repair activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium bars PMA registration.
editorial.body:
Computer repair is often treated as a small practical service, but this activity is drawn broadly. It covers the repair and maintenance of desktop computers, laptops, magnetic disk drives, removable and flash drives, printers, monitors, keyboards, mice, joysticks, trackballs, internal and external modems, computer terminals, servers, scanners—including barcode scanners—smart-card readers, virtual-reality headsets, webcams and computer projectors. The perimeter also includes repair and maintenance of non-mechanically operated ATM and point-of-sale terminals, as well as handheld computers, or PDAs. In short, it is a service activity for keeping computer equipment and associated terminals operating.

Registration is not reserved for a particular business size. The record lists the activity as open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar enterprises. That breadth matters because the classification accommodates repair and maintenance work across the stated range of computer equipment, peripherals and terminals. Its centre of gravity is the service itself: maintaining and repairing the specified computer-related equipment, from everyday devices such as laptops, printers and monitors to servers, scanners, smart-card readers and specialised terminals.

At the national level, the PMA position is unequivocally open. Foreign ownership may reach 100%, which is the stated national foreign-ownership ceiling for this activity. The position is sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a founder considering foreign investment in Indonesian computer repair and maintenance, the national setting is clear: the activity is TERBUKA and the stated PMA ceiling is 100%. The distinction between this national position and Bali’s registration outcome is essential rather than technical.

In Bali, however, a foreign-owned company cannot register this activity as PMA today. The Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO: at the Besar scale, every scope recorded for the activity is assessed in OSS as Low or Medium-Low risk, and that result is blocked by the Bali moratorium. The stated provincial rule is island-wide and permanent for PMA registrations in the Low and Medium-Low risk categories. The block is attributed to a Bali moratorium recorded in May 2026, under Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. The national 100% ceiling is real, but it does not overcome Bali’s PMA-registration block.
editorial.pullQuote: A national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling does not overcome Bali’s PMA-registration block.
